direction: Natural-language-like versus learned-vector communication for multi-robot coordination. At CPU scale: two or three simulated point robots on a 2D cooperative task (e.g. rendezvous or cooperative coverage with partial observability). Compare (a) no communication, (b) a learned continuous message vector, (c) a learned discrete token channel, and (d) a fixed, human-readable templated language of symbolic utterances (the small-scale stand-in for natural language; no LLM). Measure task success, sample efficiency and whether a receiver trained with one sender can work with another (cross-play). Be explicit that the templated language is a proxy for natural language.

decisions.decision: Chose hidden-target 2-robot rendezvous with 16-message matched-capacity channels and pathwise-gradient training for CPU feasibility; templated language = 4x4 grid row/col words, fixed speaker.

Harness matches research.yaml ablation entries to run names, so ablations are listed by system display name; the swept parameters (vocab for language/discrete, noise for continuous) are in groups sweep_vocab and sweep_noise with --config.
